back: 0 success; 1 app error; 125 docker run/daemon failed; 126 found but not executable; 127 command (or interpreter) not found.
137 SIGKILL (OOM, `docker kill`, stop timeout); 139 SIGSEGV (native crash); 143 SIGTERM (stopped, didn't handle it). Formula: 128 + signal.

front: How to tell OOM from a stop timeout (both 137)?
back: `docker inspect -f '{{.State.OOMKilled}}'` and `docker events`: `oom` then `die` vs `kill signal=15` then `kill signal=9` ~10 s later.

front: Why does PID 1 often ignore SIGTERM?
back: The kernel applies no default signal actions to PID 1 in a namespace; it must install handlers. Shells/npm as PID 1 also don't forward signals. Fix: exec-form CMD, SIGTERM handler, `--init`.
Runs tini as PID 1, which forwards signals to your process and reaps zombie processes.
Binary for another CPU architecture (arm64 vs amd64), or a script without a `#!` shebang run via exec.

front: `exec /x.sh: no such file or directory` but the file exists?
back: The shebang's interpreter is missing: CRLF line endings (`sh\r`) or `#!/bin/bash` on Alpine.
`docker debug <c>` (Docker Desktop paid) or `docker run --rm -it --pid container:<c> --network container:<c> nicolaka/netshoot`; browse files via `/proc/1/root`.

front: Default logging driver and its trap
back: `json-file`, with no rotation by default. Set `log-opts` `max-size`/`max-file` or use the `local` driver; applies to new containers.
`docker system df [-v]`, `container prune`, `image prune [-a]`, `builder prune`, `volume prune` (anonymous only unless `--all`), `system prune`.
`docker run --rm -it --entrypoint sh <image>` then run the real command by hand.

front: Which images does a tag support?
back: `docker buildx imagetools inspect <image>` lists platforms; `docker image inspect -f '{{.Architecture}}'` shows a local image's arch.
`docker stats` (CPU, memory/limit, net, block I/O, PIDs). TUIs: lazydocker, ctop.
